newsitem.title: PERU: Andean Pact sees Dec Mercosur preliminary accord.
newsitem.headline: Andean Pact sees Dec Mercosur preliminary accord.

text.p: The five-nation Andean pact group said Tuesday it expects to sign a prelimianry accord over a free-trade pact with South America's largest trade bloc, the Mercosur customs union.

"We are going to start work on a shared negotiation," Bolivia's foreign minister Antonio Aranibar told reporters. "In December in a meeting in Brazil an accord setting out the framework for integration will be signed."
Aranibar was speaking after a meeting of the Andean Pact foreign ministers to discuss how to carry out negotiations over the free-trade pact with Mercosur.
In a press release, the Andean Pact group announced that its foreign ministers had agreed at the meeting on a policy to establish the free-trade zone within 10 years and "earlier in special cases."
Earlier this month, at the Rio Group of Latin American nations, the Andean Pact group announced it had started talks with Mercosur over creating a possible free-trade area.
The Andean Pact groups Colombia, Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela, while the Mercosur customs union groups Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
A free-trade area between the two blocs would encompass around 300 million consumers.
Both Venezuela and Peru are already individually negotiating free-trade pacts with Mercosur, which they have said they expect to conclude by the end of the year.
The two blocs have agreed with other countries in the continent to create a region-wide free-trade zone by 2005.
Virtually all Latin American countries have now cast aside protectionist and isolationist practices of the past, adopting regional economic integration.
